correctness.rationale: Exact affine orthogonal-projection normal equations give a unique diagonal zero coordinate. The symmetric Fejér block consists of two products of geometric kernels at distinct boundary points; diagonal terms have leading moments \(2m(m+1)\overline{(a+b)}\) and \(2(m+1)^2|a+b|^2\), with cross terms uniformly bounded by nonresonant geometric sums. Therefore its Hardy moment ratio converges to \((a+b)/2\), which can be an arbitrary nonzero interior target. Adding a uniformly small high-degree shift of this block to 1 makes a zero-free polynomial. Normalizing high-degree weighted coefficients by \(N^{2lpha}\) kills the constant contribution precisely when \(lpha>0\), and transfers the target ratio. The origin follows by approximating nonzero targets. The explicit Python coefficient checker passed; no finite test was used as a proof.

value.rationale: A natural location problem for the zeros of optimal polynomial approximants remains after known constructions give only a fixed interior example for each positive Dirichlet parameter. Density in the entire disk diagonal, even with symmetry and closed-bidisk zero-free input, is an infinite qualitative flexibility phenomenon that strictly strengthens mere existence. It permits zeros arbitrarily close to the origin at every positive weight. The Hardy endpoint and exact-realization problem are expressly not claimed.
